title.narrative: Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises Line of Credit Project

description.narrative: The proposed project is a line of credit to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Sri Lanka with an innovative feature of allocating loan proceeds to participating financial institutions (PFIs) via an auction system. The project also includes an attached technical assistance (TA) for export-oriented cluster development to develop Sri Lanka's next generation of SMEs.

Progress Toward Outcome: a. Completed. $209.35 million were lent to the targeted SMEs as of 30 September 2022.b. Completed. The report was endorsed by the steering committee in 2016. The proposal is included in COBP as 2022 firm project.c. Completed. Cluster-based loan to a tea cluster was financed in 2020.d. Completed. Out of 557 women entrepreneurs who completed the JFPR training, 398 submitted business plans which were considered as viable by banks (71.4%). Out of 470 women entrepreneurs who completed the We-Fi training, 395 submitted business plans which were considered as viable by banks (84.0%).e. Completed. $41.4 million of blended finance provided to SMEs that are led by women as of 30 September 2022.f. On track. To be evaluated after the full disbursement of We-Fi grant in 2022. The baseline survey was initiated in 2019.g. On track. $6.17 million was provided to tea smallholders as of 30 September 2022. h. On track. The TA is preparing a design for the mobile application platform. i. Completed. 3483 SMEs affected by COVID-19 accessed the affordable working capital credit line as of 30 September 2022. (Out of such 454 SMEs were led by women as of 30 June 2022)
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Aug 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/49273/49273-001-apfs-en_71.pdf
Some results are in the Environment and Social Management System Arrangements | Dec 2017: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/49273/49273-001-esms-en_3.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: 1a. On track. $ 214.5 million was disbursed to participating banks as of 30 September 2022. 1b. On track with delay. $8.2 million was disbursed to participating banks as of 30 September 2022.1c. Completed. 963 women-led SMEs accessed We-Fi grant financing as of 30 September 2022.1d. On track. $ 0.50 million of JFPR grant funding was disbursed to participating banks as of 30 September 2022. 1e. Completed.623 tea smallholders accessed JFPR grant as of 30 September 2022.1f. Completed. $ 100 million was disbursed to PFIs as of 30 September 2022.1g. On track. A plan for using reflow will be proposed towards the end of 2022.2a. Completed. The two auctions were carried out in 2016. 2b. Completed. A report on a national credit guarantee scheme for SMEs was submitted to the steering committee in 2016. 3a. Completed. One cluster-based loan to fruits and vegetable cluster was presented to a bank in 2017 and another cluster-based loan to tea cluster was presented to a bank in 2020. 3b. Completed. 1,027 female entrepreneurs from various sectors were trained in business development and management (out of which, 557 were trained under the JFPR and 470 were trained under the We-Fi) as of 30 June 2022.3c. Completed. Online platform for learning, mentoring and networking is being developed. As the first stage, the platform was used to conduct the online trainings for women SMEs from April 2021. 514 women entrepreneurs were registered in the platform as of 30 September 2022. Partner onboarding activities were carried out.3d. On track. The TA is preparing a design for the mobile application platform. Consultants started the stakeholder discussions. 3e. On track with delay. Pilot training programes were started in March. 102 tea smallholders , including 22 women were trained on financial literacy.3f. On track. Consulation with the PFIs started in Q1 2022. 3g. On track. Started receiving financial records as of 30 September 2022.4a. Completed. The national brand for ICT-BPM sector ('Island of Ingenuity ) was launched on 15 February 2018.4b. Completed. Two career events were held with 1641 female student participation in 2018. 4c. On track with a delay. A consultant was recruited in 2021 and work will commence in 2022.5a. Completed. Gender gap assessment reports and draft action plans were approved by the 3 government agencies (Industrial Development Board, Industrial Technology Institute, National Entrepreneurship Development Board). 5b. Completed. Final Gender Gap Assessment reports (inclusive of action plans) were shared with the National Chamber of Commerce of Sri Lanka and Federation of Chambers of Commerce of Sri Lanka in Q1 2022.5c. Completed. Training materials and surveys were developed. Trainings were conducted for 216 staff of 3 government agencies.6 63.4% of the persons surveyed developed action plans to support women entrepreneurs and reported higher level of awareness of gender specific challenges.5d. Completed. Individual gender gap assessment reports along with recommendations were shared and presented to 10 Participating Financial Institutions (PFIs). The Boards of directors of all10 PFIs have endorsed the reports and recommendations as of 31 May 2021. In addition, Gender Gap Assessment for the new 3 banks (Pan Asia, Sanasa and Union) were completed as of 30 September 2022.Gender awareness workshop was conducted in Q3 2022 for 13 PFI officers with the participation of the officers of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka and Ministry of Finance. 6a. On track with delay. Impact evaluation on the effectiveness of business development trainings is being undertaken from 2019.6b. Substantially Completed. Final policy paper on microfinance for women was submitted to the government in December 2021and it was endorsed by the MOF and the Central Bank. 6c. On track with delay. One national seminar on access to finance was held in partnership with Women's Chamber of Industry and Commerce Sri Lanka (WCIC) on 10 September 2019 with 100 women entrepreneur participation. Other seminars/webinars are planned for the later stage of the We-Fi grant project implementation.Gender awareness workshop was conducted in Q3 2022 for 13 PFI officers with the participation of the officers of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka and Ministry of Finance.
